subject: Acme - Discovery & bake-off criteria (recap)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Priya Gupta <priya.gupta@acme.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>, Ben Torres <ben.torres@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Jul 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme - Discovery & bake-off criteria (recap)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Great to meet earlier today. Thanks for the time and context — below is a quick recap of what we heard, success criteria you called out, and suggested bake-off acceptance criteria so the team can align. Please flag anything I missed.

TL;DR
- Pain: inconsistent p95 latency during spikes, high per-token cost on cloud for production, and operational burden of self-hosted model upgrades.
- Current stack: self-hosted TGI on k8s for baseline workloads, experimenting with vLLM for latency-sensitive inference, and using OpenAI endpoints for peak traffic.
- Success criteria: comparable/better latency at target throughput, cost <= current baseline, and no degradation in generation quality on our eval set.

1) Pain points (from call)
- Unpredictable tail latency on long-context generations during concurrent load.
- Cost volatility when falling back to cloud endpoints for spikes.
- Ops overhead: patching kernels, manual batching, and cache priming.

2) Current stack (as described)
- TGI on k8s (prod baseline)
- vLLM experiments for warm-cache low-latency workloads
- OpenAI endpoints for burst capacity and gen fallback

3) Proposed success criteria for bake-off
- Latency: 95th percentile request latency <= 250ms for 512-token responses at 20 RPS sustained (warm cache).
- Throughput: sustain at least 10k tokens/sec aggregated across the cluster under realistic prompt mix.
- Quality: >= 90% pass rate on your 50 prompt eval set (we'll use the shared prompts you mentioned).
- Cost: estimated per-1M token cost (hosted + Dedicated comparisons) must be <= your current blended cost.
- Reliability: graceful fallback to model variants with <1% error rate during simulated capacity pressure.

4) Bake-off scope & comparisons
- We'll run side-by-side on: Redwood-hosted endpoint (standard runtime), Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity), vLLM self-hosted, TGI self-hosted, and OpenAI (cloud) endpoints for reference.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, cold vs warm start, model quality (your eval), and unit cost.

5) Benchmarks / data we need from you
- Representative eval set (50 prompts) — ideally the examples you use for user-facing flows.
- Typical response length distribution and concurrency targets (you mentioned 512 tokens median; confirm).
- Any compliance/data residency constraints (you mentioned EU customers, but primary traffic is US).

6) Next steps
- Sean (cc'd) will send a benchmark runbook + configuration matrix and propose dates for a 2-week bake-off.
- Marissa will share the bake-off template and SOC 2 summary (attachments).
- Acme to confirm the eval prompts and target date window.

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-template.xlsx (template for test cases), SOC2-summary.pdf

Thanks — happy to sync with your infra team on specifics.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

---
Note: attached files are templates/summary stubs; final runbook and configs from Sean in follow-up.

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Gupta <priya.gupta@acme.com>, Ben Torres <ben.torres@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Jul 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - Discovery & bake-off criteria (recap)

Thanks Marissa — this looks right. A few clarifications / asks from our side:

- Confirm our current baseline: TGI on a 4-node k8s cluster (NVIDIA A10s) for production, with vLLM experiments on p4 instances. OpenAI used only for high-volume spikes.
- Response length: median 450 tokens, 95th ~900 tokens. The 512 number in your template is fine for the first pass, but we'd like a second run using the 900-token tail to validate long-context behavior.
- Quality metric: can you define "pass rate" — is that semantic equivalence / BLEU-like scoring or human review? We prefer a mix: automated similarity score threshold + 10 human-verified examples.
- Data residency: primary production in US, but any logs/eval artifacts must stay in the US or on our VPC. Please confirm Redwood Dedicated / Private options for EU if needed.

Timeline: we want the bake-off started the week of Jul 15 if possible (2-week window).

Also: we'll need an NDA before we share the eval dataset and some of the internal prompts. Can you send?

Appreciate it — look forward to the runbook.

— Alex
Alex Johnson
Director of ML Platforms | Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Priya Gupta <priya.gupta@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Torres <ben.torres@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Jul 2026 11:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - Discovery & bake-off criteria (recap)

Thanks Alex — quick technical follow-up and proposed benchmark plan.

Proposed benchmark runbook (high level):
1) Datasets / prompts\   - 50 representative prompts (you provide)\   - Two length buckets: ~512 tokens and ~900 tokens (to validate the long-context tail)
2) Test matrix\   - Redwood hosted (latest runtime)\   - Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool; config will mirror your region)\   - vLLM self-hosted (your config)\   - TGI self-hosted (your baseline)\   - OpenAI / cloud endpoint (reference)
3) Metrics captured\   - p50/p95/p99 latency (request-level)\   - tokens/sec (aggregate)\   - cold vs warm cache behavior (measure 1st request vs steady-state)\   - error rates and rare failure modes\   - qualitative scoring: automated embedding similarity + 10 human-verified checks
4) Acceptance criteria (concrete)\   - p95 <= 250ms at 20 RPS for 512-token bucket (warm)\   - p95 <= 700ms at 5 RPS for 900-token bucket (warm)\   - >=90% automated pass rate and 8/10 human checks pass\   - cost estimates provided as $/1M tokens for each configuration\5) Logistics\   - We'll provide a runbook and a small benchmarking script (no binary attachments in email) — attaching the runbook stub: benchmark-runbook.md\   - For Dedicated tests we can provision a reserved pool in us-west-2 to mirror your infra. For your self-hosted runs we'll provide a dockerized runner and recommended instance types.\   - We'll need a contact on your infra team for SSH/key exchange if you want us to run end-to-end on your cluster (optional).

Open items for you:
- NDA (Marissa can send DocuSign)\- Eval prompts + sample traffic distribution\- Confirmation of target start date (week of Jul 15)

I'll follow up with the detailed runbook and a concrete calendar invite for the kickoff once NDA is in place.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.ai
+1 (650) 555-0124
